items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Mr. Chipman, who played a cello, and he used to play the bass parts in church with the piano, and him on cello, and the people in church would play the tambourine and the bass drum, so that's how I came in

ctx.x: So I joined St. Agnes' band, too, so I was playing with the UNIA band and I also was playing with St. Agnes' band.

And then from there, there was a man that lived a couple of doors down from us that belonged to the Church of God, Mr. Chipman, who played a cello, and he used to play the bass parts in church with the piano, and him on cello, and the people in church would play the tambourine and the bass drum, so that's how I came in -- I used to play the bass drum on Sundays, although I belonged to the Roman Catholic faith, that was my gig on Sunday -- I used to go to the church and play, and I used to get 50¢ for playing…

So anyway, we also used to play for the -- when they got baptized, we used to have to march from, like, 5th and Court Corbin and 17th Street to where the church was, to almost Miami Beach where the water was, and that's where they had the Baptisms there, and we used to march back to the church from there.
